clue.text: Detective emerging from helicopter with our suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not genuine, so the letters before it are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A sleuth climbs out of a helicopter, accompanied by the man we suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' reads as the person the detective is after, but it is the anagram signal; 'emerging from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's Belgian sleuth is one of fiction's best-known investigators.

clue.text: Graduates seen cavorting outside, all together

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters sit around the graduates, enclosing them
cavorting means prancing about, so the letters of seen jump into a new order

parts.note: MAs are Masters of Arts, holders of a higher degree

explanation.surface: A group of new graduates is spotted dancing about outdoors, all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like a place for the cavorting, but it is the container signal; 'cavorting' makes ENSE, which then wraps the degree holders.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase describes people acting as one body, in a crowd at the same time.

clue.text: Boasted in company

definitions.meaning: an old past tense of crow, to brag the way a cockerel does
a team or body of people working together, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Someone bragged while among friends.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the rarer past tense of crow (crowed or the older form), which is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's or film's workforce is a company of people; a cockerel's past boasting is an old form of crowed.

clue.text: Young son scatters rubbish untidily about

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals born together

explanation.surface: A boy throws waste carelessly around the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young' looks like an adjective for the son, but it is the noun: a set of newborn animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop waste messily across a place is the verb sense of strewing refuse.

clue.text: Customers of SPAR not fickle

indicators.note: fickle means changeable and unsteady, so the letters of the two words switch places

explanation.surface: Shoppers at the SPAR convenience chain are loyal, not changeable.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAR is a convenience-store chain in Britain and elsewhere; the capitals are only surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular shoppers or clients of a business are its customers.

clue.text: Country, near ruin at intervals, that's on the rise

indicators.note: on the rise in a down clue means the picked letters are read upwards, bottom to top
at intervals means taking every other letter of the two words, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A nation teetering on ruin now and then shows signs of recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes NARI from NEAR RUIN; 'on the rise' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern nation once called Persia is a sovereign state.

clue.text: Confess on purpose action proving personally disadvantageous

parts.note: to own up, or simply own, is to admit or confess
a goal is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Admitting things deliberately is a move that backfires on you.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stretches the football idea: scoring into your own net is any act that harms yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, putting the ball in your own net helps the opponents; figuratively, any self-inflicted setback.

clue.text: Standard conversation in market with traders

parts.note: stock as an adjective means standard or regular, as in a stock reply
an exchange is a conversation or back-and-forth of words

explanation.surface: A routine chat takes place in a busy marketplace among dealers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bourse is a marketplace where dealers buy and sell shares.

clue.text: Sound almost excited feeding small, sad-looking tree

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the sound and the trimmed word go inside the other pair

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
low means downcast or sad
a ping is a short high sound, as from a phone alert

indicators.note: almost says the word for excited loses its last letter

parts.note: wild means frantically excited

explanation.surface: A noise, nearly frantic, nourishes a small, melancholy-looking tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad-looking' seems part of the definition but belongs to the wordplay; 'almost' drops a final letter, and 'feeding' sends the sound and trimmed word into the middle of the outer pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow with drooping branches is a familiar species of tree beside rivers.

clue.text: Trial engulfs European politician in storm

indicators.note: engulfs means swallows up, so the word for trial surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a test is a trial
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A court case swallows up a Euro politician in a political storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent gale with heavy wind and rain is a tempestuous weather event, a synonym of storm.

clue.text: Student requiring support to install shower

indicators.note: to install means to put in place, so the word for shower goes inside the support

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: A student needs some help putting a shower in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' suggests bathroom plumbing, but here it is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone learning a trade or job is a learner, a kind of student.

clue.text: Detected by auditors, hiding-place for money

indicators.note: auditors are also listeners, so what they detect is what is heard, a word said aloud

parts.note: a cache is a secret store or hiding place

explanation.surface: Accountants find a secret stash of funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' looks like the accountants, but it means listeners, signalling a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes and coins are ready funds, the everyday sense of money.

clue.text: Spirit voice

definitions.meaning: the general drift or underlying sense of something
a male singing voice above baritone

explanation.definitionFit: The gist of a document is its underlying sense; and in music it names a high male singing part.

clue.text: TV show that gets one into a lather?

definitions.text: TV show that gets one into a lather?

parts.words: TV show that gets one into a lather?
parts.note: a serial drama gets viewers worked up, and a bar of the cleaning product makes a foamy lather

explanation.surface: A television programme that gets you all worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: These serials were first sponsored in the US by detergent makers, hence their name and the double sense of lather.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running domestic television drama shares its name with the foaming cleaner, after its original sponsors.

clue.text: One granting wishes of a German, say, to go north

indicators.note: to go north in a down clue means reading the letters upwards

parts.note: ein is German for a
eg (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: Someone grants the wishes of a German heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a German' is the German word for 'a', not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The spirit from the lamp in Aladdin famously grants three wishes.

clue.text: Not entirely neglect fashion

indicators.note: not entirely says the word for neglect is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to forget is to neglect

explanation.surface: Don't completely ignore the world of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' reads as the clothing world, but it is a verb: to shape or make.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape metal by heating and hammering, or to make generally, is to fashion it.

clue.text: Cricket teams in prime fitness at last

parts.note: eleven is a prime number

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word fitness

explanation.surface: Cricket sides finally reach peak physical condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime fitness' reads as one phrase, but 'prime' is a prime number. A cricket side has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket sides field eleven players each, so the teams are named after that number.

clue.text: Fifty tucking into hot Christmas food

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the numeral sits within the word for hot

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people tuck into warm festive fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it puts L inside STOLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A German fruit loaf dusted with sugar is traditional festive baking.

clue.text: Club perhaps provided source of financial capital

parts.note: a club is one of the four suits, so a club is an example of a playing card
if means provided that

indicators.note: source of picks the first letter of financial

explanation.surface: A golf or social club might be a source of financial capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'financial capital' reads as funds; the capital is a city. This one is the capital of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh seat of government is a capital city.

clue.text: Dish, excessive starter of olives, gentleman served up

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the pieces are written bottom to top

parts.note: OTT is over the top, excessive

indicators.note: starter of picks the first letter of olives

parts.note: sir is a title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman is served a dish with too many olives to start.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice preparation cooked in stock is a dish.

clue.text: Zealot is in fact a criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A zealous man is, in truth, a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is an extremist with obsessive enthusiasm for a cause.

clue.text: Exhibition of setter's skills displayed here?

definitions.text: Exhibition of setter's skills displayed here?

parts.words: Exhibition of setter's skills displayed here?
parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog, not a crossword compiler, and such breeds are judged at shows

explanation.surface: Where a crossword compiler might show off their talents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' wants to be the crossword setter; it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeds such as the Irish setter are judged in a canine competition.

clue.text: Article of furniture, one found backstage in theatre

definitions.meaning: a kitchen sideboard with shelves for plates
a theatre assistant who helps actors with costumes

explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh-style sideboard holds crockery; in theatre the word names the costume helper.

clue.text: Reportedly Berlin chap's address has identity code that secures locks

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the German title is replaced by a word sounding like it

parts.note: Herr is the German form of address for a man, like Mr
a PIN is a personal identification number

explanation.surface: A Berlin man's home address includes a code that secures his locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a street address, but it is a form of address, the German title. 'locks' are tresses of hair, not door fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped clip holds tresses in place, securing a hairdo.

clue.text: A little optional something in addition

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small extra that you can take or leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means too or as well, adding one thing to another.

clue.text: Single redundant worker being released

indicators.note: being released says the worker is let go, taken out of the longer word

parts.note: redundant means no longer needed, unwanted
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A lone employee made redundant is let go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' and 'released' look like one sacking, but the worker is an ant removed from UNWANTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone never married is single, a synonym in the marital sense.

clue.text: Herb swallowed finally with difficulty

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of swallowed

parts.note: ill means badly or with difficulty, as in one can ill afford it

explanation.surface: A herb finally got down, but only with difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL as an adverb meaning scarcely or with difficulty is a less familiar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A feathery plant used for flavouring fish and pickles is a culinary herb.

clue.text: Quarrel that's quick blows over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for quick blows is reversed

parts.note: taps are light, quick blows

explanation.surface: A row that's brief soon blows over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows over' reads as dying down, but 'blows' belongs with 'quick' and 'over' is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty argument or squabble is a brief fallout between people.

clue.text: High time Rosalind essentially left

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence or heart, so take the central letters of Rosalind

explanation.surface: It's high time Rosalind left.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosalind has eight letters, so its heart is the middle two, AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lofty building is one of great height, as is a lanky person.

clue.text: Energy needed by snooker player possibly in decline

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
what a snooker player needs to do is sink balls, to pot them

explanation.surface: A snooker player in a slump may need more energy.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, a player scores by potting balls into the pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for falling into ruin or deteriorating badly describes something sliding downhill.

clue.text: Mum loves employing rag mop regularly as cleaner

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the quiet and loves surround the picked letters

parts.note: mum as in keep mum means quiet, signalled by sh
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like the letter O, so two loves are OO

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of rag mop

explanation.surface: Mother loves using a mop as a cleaning tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means quiet. 'regularly' picks AMP from RAG MOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid soap for washing hair or carpets is a cleansing product.

clue.text: State running Austrian school, having sacked Head

indicators.note: running means flowing or loose, so the letters move into a new order
having sacked its head means the word school loses its first letter

explanation.surface: An Austrian school is being run after its headteacher was fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the headteacher, but it is the first letter of 'school'. The letters of AUSTRIAN and CHOOL, shuffled together, give the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleston and Columbia lie in this southeastern US state.
